body:
Building something is one thing. Getting your first real users is a whole different challenge 🚀 

If you've launched a site, app, or product, how did you get your first real users? 👀 

What actually worked for you?

#BuildInPublic #IndieHackers #Startups #WebDevelopment
note: Hashtag engagement question to an audience ('what worked for you?') from an affiliate account, not someone stuck.

body:
My first 5 Posthero customers all came from content.

Not ads. Not cold outreach. Not a launch. Just posts on X and LinkedIn.

Here's the part people don't expect: 

I had around 400 followers on X at the time. 
That's nothing. No viral posts, no big audience, no algorithm hacks.
note: Founder broadcasting how their own product (Posthero) got customers - a success story promoting a product, not a need.

body:
July 2026: My side project finally got its first paying customer. Duration: 14 months. Revenue: $47/month. But the difference from before: I now know who pays and why. That's worth more than 1000 beta testers.

#buildinpublic #indiedev #solopreneur #tech
note: Build-in-public milestone celebrating a first paying customer - nothing unsolved is described.

body:
If you're stuck at 10k/month

Pick ONE. Go all in:

1. Cold outreach
2. Warm outreach
3. Ads
4. Content

Then:

1. 99% ignore the rest
2. Do better
3. Do more
3. Repeat 10,000 times
4. Get feedback
5. Never stop

Focus + volume + iteration + time

Simple idea. Hard to do.
note: Growth advice aimed at others ('Pick ONE') - the author is teaching, not asking.

body: 2) Problem posts: reply in communities with a short, specific fix and an ask. Cold outreach micro-test: 3 emails to founders who recently posted the problem, subject: "Two quick fixes for [problem]". Body: one diagnostic sentence, one quick fix, one tiny ask (15-min call).
note: A how-to thread on cold outreach written for other founders - advice content, not a founder with the problem.

body: I think it's just a bad business. You have to keep selling to new buildings, no subscription. Customer acquisition cost (travel, schmoozing, installation support) high. Each sale, you better sell a ton of these at $150 each.

body: Simple idea. Hard to do. There are only 4 ways to get a customer. Cold outreach, warm outreach, ads, content. Everything you've ever read about marketing is a sub-layer of one of those 4. Focus + volume + iteration + time.
note: Generic framework post about the four acquisition channels - advice, not a need.

body:
You started in the middle. There's an order.

    1. Choose an idea
    2. Validate the problem
    3. Create an offer
    4. Build one page
    5. Find first customers
    6. Sell + follow up
    7. Improve what worked
    8. Make it repeatable
    9. Plan next 30 days
note: Step-by-step startup advice list aimed at others.
